subject: About about the CPO and in-sample fit

messages.author: bd6d05f06437885c
messages.subject: About about the CPO and in-sample fit
parts:
Hi Help,
 
When I am fitting a surface with the inla.spde2.matern model in inla, I found a confusing thing. 
Basically, I fit the data with spde model, and calculate the error between the fitted values and the observations (at the same locations, in-sample estimate goodness) and calculate the cpo (as in the FAQ) to measure the predictive fit goodness.
The data z is of scale around -130 ~ 90,
1) if I use z in the inla, then I get all the cpo$failure are 0 (and resonable cpo values), but the in-sample estimate error are large (MSE of around 87) 
2) if I use z/20 (which should be of order 1) in the inla, then I get nearly perfect in-sample estimate (MSE of order 1e-7), but all the cpo$failure are 1.. (most of the cpo$cpo are of order 1e-9...)
In addition, in some trials, it seems that the mesh strucure also has some effect on the cpo$failure (and cpo$cpo itself). 
Could you explain why this happens and what should I do to deal with these confusing situation? I also attached the script and data with this post in case you need a quick run to see the results.
Thanks a lot!
 
Best regards,
David

>> The data z is of scale around -130 ~ 90,

The default prior for the variance of the spde2.matern model is centered at 1, with a default uncertainty that may be too low for your data variance.
See
http://www.r-inla.org/examples/tutorials/spde-tutorial-from-jss
which contains some discussion about how to change the default prior.

If your results depend strongly on the mesh you probably have either a too coarse mesh, or a mesh with some clustered nodes. Make sure that you use the "cutoff" parameter when building the mesh (see the same link above) and also inspect the generated mesh visually.

Finn

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] About about the CPO and in-sample fit
parts:
Hi Havard and Finn,
 
Thanks for your suggestion! As in the paper Finn mentioned said, the prior may be very important when spde model is just a smoother which is just my case.
In the spde model, x ~ N(0,Q^(-1)), eta = Ax, and in my simple case z~N(eta,sigma2).. if z is rescale to z/10, does that mean the sd (corresponding to log(sigma) in the paper) of x is kind of shrinked so that we need a prior for which small sd is more likely? 
Also in the paper it is said "Experimental helper functions for constructing parameterisations and priors are included in the package", but it seems not mention which specific functions are helpful in exploring the appropriate priors?
 
Many thanks!
David
